summary: Prioritize everyday chemical phenomena over abstract biological or physical mechanics to drive immediate viewer retention.
Formulate hooks that immediately challenge common assumptions rather than asking generic open-ended questions.
Eliminate overly wordy hypothetical scenarios from the opening sentence to reduce friction in the critical swipe-away window.
Keep video durations under 40 seconds to prevent natural drop-off points from ruining the average view percentage.
Incorporate specific physical actions or visual triggers into the title instead of generic academic labels.
winning_hooks: Why does baking soda fizz the moment it hits vinegar?
avoid: You've used soap your whole life, but why does it clean grease when plain water fails?
A 10kg lead sphere and a 1kg lead sphere dropped from the same height in a vacuum. Why don't they hit the ground at different moments?
next_experiment: Test if starting a physics video with a direct, single-sentence question ('Why do heavy things fall at the same speed as light things?') increases stayed_pct above 40% compared to using a complex hypothetical scenario.
